sample_plan.subpopulation_description: U.S. resident aged 0–4, including infants and very young children whose daily needs are shaped by caregivers and developmental stage.
U.S. residents aged 5–14, school-age children and young teenagers with needs and activities shaped by development and caregivers; this band excludes infants.
U.S. residents aged 5–14, school-age children and young teenagers with varied developmental stages and caregiver involvement; this band excludes infants.
U.S. residents aged 15–17, older adolescents navigating education and changing family or social roles; work and leisure characteristics are left open for this age range.
U.S. residents aged 18–24 who are employed and participating in the labor force; this young-adult group spans education, early employment, and changing family or social roles.
U.S. residents aged 18–24 who are not currently participating in the labor force; this young-adult group includes varied education and family circumstances.
U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: warm and cooperative, with contrasting food, shopping, wellbeing, cultural, travel, and lifestyle preferences drawn independently.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: generally pessimistic but warm in interpersonal style, with varied food, shopping, health, product, cultural, travel, and lifestyle choices.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: open to unfamiliar viewpoints and intellectually curious, with a distinct mix of food, shopping, health, cultural, travel, and lifestyle characteristics.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: emotionally mixed under pressure, with a vegetarian culinary preference and distinct wellbeing, product, cultural, travel, and lifestyle characteristics.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: positive and appreciative, with a plant-based culinary preference and varied education, health, cultural, travel, and lifestyle characteristics.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: sociable and energetic, with a meat-centered culinary preference and independent shopping, health, product, cultural, travel, and lifestyle traits.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: pragmatically hopeful, with traditional culinary preferences and a distinct mix of work, shopping, wellbeing, cultural, travel, and lifestyle characteristics.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: welcoming but cautious about trust, with convenient-food preferences and varied shopping, health, cultural, travel, and lifestyle characteristics.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: apathetic or disengaged, with a restrictive diet and varied financial, health, cultural, travel, technology, and lifestyle characteristics.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in a behavioral-contrast allocation: unusually hostile and closed-minded in disagreement, while other personality, food, shopping, health, product, cultural, travel, and lifestyle dimensions remain independently specified.
U.S. resident aged 25–54 allocated solely to guarantee a strongly progressive political-belief profile; other political affiliations and public-opinion responses remain open to supplied alternatives.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 allocated solely to guarantee a strongly conservative political-belief profile; other political affiliations and public-opinion responses remain open to supplied alternatives.
U.S. resident aged 25–54 allocated to represent limited or interrupted formal schooling and literacy support needs, without additional personality, political, or leisure assumptions.
U.S. resident aged 25–54 allocated to represent advanced education and broad intellectual expertise; no additional personality, political, or leisure assumptions are imposed.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in an illustrative multigenerational White non-Hispanic cultural-background cell; the matched broad race/ethnicity category is selected without additional cultural or political assumptions.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in an illustrative Mexican-origin or other Mexican American cultural-background cell, paired with the Hispanic or Latino category and without additional assumptions about beliefs or preferences.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in an illustrative multigenerational African American cultural-background cell, paired with the Black or African American category and without additional personality or political assumptions.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in an illustrative East Asian American cultural-background cell, paired with the Asian category and without additional assumptions about education, income, politics, or tastes.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in an illustrative multiracial cultural-background cell, paired with the two-or-more-races category; the profile does not imply any further demographic or attitudinal correlation.

U.S. resident aged 25–54 in an illustrative American Indian or Alaska Native cultural-background cell, paired with the corresponding supplied category and without added assumptions about lifestyle or beliefs.
U.S. resident aged 55–64, representing people approaching retirement or navigating midlife career, health, and household transitions.
U.S. residents aged 55–64, with varied work, household, education, and transition circumstances represented within this supplied age band.
U.S. resident aged 65 or older, representing an older adult with advanced specialist expertise; health, mobility, work, and support needs remain varied within this age band.
U.S. residents aged 65 or older, including active older adults and people with varied health, mobility, caregiving, and support needs.
U.S. residents aged 65 or older, with varied household, work, health, and support circumstances represented within the supplied older-adult band.
